note: Literature establishes TBC1D32 involvement in ciliopathies including OFD type IX, syndromic hypopituitarism, and retinal/ciliary phenotypes overlapping Joubert and Pallister-Hall syndromes.

evidence.text: TBC1D32 is expressed in the developing hypothalamus and pituitary gland and associated with severe ciliary anomalies, hypopituitarism, and orofaciodigital syndrome type IX.

source.title: Diagnosis of TBC1D32-associated conditions
source.quote: TBC1D32 is involved in the development and function of cilia and is expressed in the developing hypothalamus and pituitary gland.

evidence.text: TBC1D32 loss-of-function variants underlie syndromic hypopituitarism and orofaciodigital syndrome type IX.

source.title: Confirming TBC1D32‐related ciliopathy in humans
source.quote: Loss-of-Function Variants in TBC1D32 Underlie Syndromic Hypopituitarism · Ciliary Genes TBC1D32/C6orf170 and SCLT1 are Mutated in Patients with OFD Type IX.
